smells.finding: spec_shape_faults (scripts/generate_spine.py:145-217, 72 lines incl. blanks/docstring) does five distinct fault categories (duplicate-gate-id, missing-field, gated-missing-postconditions, all-qualitative-postconditions, config-ref-not-json) inline in one function, where validate_spine.py -- the file DESIGN_NOTE.md section 8 explicitly names as this module's own precedent for the pure/impure split -- gives each fault category its own `_fault_*` function called from one small dispatcher. Not blocking: the checks share mutable local state accumulated across one pass over gates/conditions (seen_gate_ids, pre_ids, post_ids), so splitting would either re-walk the gate list per check or thread that state across functions awkwardly. Worth a maintainer's attention if a sixth fault category is added.

_probe_pytest/_probe_script/_probe_population (scripts/generate_spine.py:402,444,481) all take the identical (gid, cid, cond, *, repo_root) parameter group and each independently re-derives `where = f"{gid}.{cid}"` on its own first line. validate_spine.py's own sibling `_fault_*` functions (e.g. _fault_zero_collect(where, check, repo_root), _fault_artifact_no_match(where, cond, check)) take a pre-built `where` instead, per-call, once -- the precedent this module is designed to match (DESIGN_NOTE.md section 8) computes `where` once and passes it down rather than recomputing it three times. Not blocking: functionally identical, and no documented repo standard mandates one form over the other, so this is a minor style divergence from precedent, not a defect.

The closed CHECK_KINDS vocabulary and RESERVED_CONDITION_ID are deliberate closures against future untyped extension, the opposite of speculative generality -- no unused hook, no configurability added ahead of a second caller.
